violated_contract: A user's bulk delete of recordings must itself establish the quiescence it needs, then report what is actually gone. Manage Storage > Clear asked each store to delete while the independent pendant ring drain and the upload pass kept running. RingStorageSyncImpl refuses a ring clear while a read is active and only logs it; the drain restarts by itself, so the user had no reliable way to stop it first. A 3.0.21 pendant with 11 h unread therefore could not be cleared, Clear All still toasted success without re-reading any store, and Clear Pending also removed uploads the server had accepted but not settled.
canonical_prevention: SyncProvider.clearStorage owns every Manage Storage clear. For audio that is not uploaded it takes a WalSyncs clear hold (cancel ring drain and upload pass; block ring wakes, coordinator drain and discovery, and manual syncs), waits bounded for reads to settle, aborts rather than deleting around a transfer that will not stop, deletes from a target snapshot taken after the stop, re-reads every store (ring matched by device), releases the hold in finally and wakes transfers once. Tests run a clear against an active and an unstoppable pendant read.
